title: Psalms Chapter 115 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 115 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 115 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 115.

questions.question: What should be given to the name of the LORD according to Psalms 115:1?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'Not unto us, O LORD, not unto us, but unto thy name give glory...' indicating that glory is to be given to the Lord's name.

questions.question: According to Psalms 115:2, what do the heathen question?
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly states, 'Wherefore should the heathen say, Where is now their God?' indicating their question about God's presence.

questions.question: Where is our God according to Psalms 115:3?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'But our God is in the heavens...' confirming that God is located in the heavens.

questions.question: What materials are the idols made of according to Psalms 115:4?
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states, 'Their idols are silver and gold, the work of men's hands,' identifying the materials used for idols.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 115:5, idols have mouths but cannot speak.
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'They have mouths, but they speak not,' confirming that idols cannot speak.

questions.question: According to Psalms 115:6, idols have ears but what do they not do?
questions.explanation: The verse says, 'They have ears, but they hear not,' indicating that idols cannot hear.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 115:7 states that idols have hands that can handle.
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'They have hands, but they handle not,' indicating that idols cannot handle anything.

questions.question: What is said about those who make idols in Psalms 115:8?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'They that make them are like unto them,' indicating that those who create idols become similar to them.

questions.question: According to Psalms 115:9, who should trust in the LORD?
questions.explanation: The verses encourage trust in the LORD from various groups: Israel, the house of Aaron, and those who fear the LORD.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 115:12 states that the LORD has forgotten the house of Israel.
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'The LORD hath been mindful of us,' indicating that the LORD has not forgotten them.

questions.question: What will the LORD do for those who fear Him according to Psalms 115:13?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'He will bless them that fear the LORD,' confirming that the LORD will bless those who fear Him.

questions.question: According to Psalms 115:14, what will the LORD do for you and your children?
options: He shall increase you more and more
questions.correctAnswer: He shall increase you more and more
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'The LORD shall increase you more and more, you and your children,' indicating growth and blessing.

questions.question: What are the heavens said to belong to in Psalms 115:16?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'The heaven, even the heavens, are the LORD'S,' indicating that the heavens belong to the LORD.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 115:18 ends with a declaration to praise the LORD forevermore.
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'But we will bless the LORD from this time forth and for evermore,' confirming the commitment to praise the LORD eternally.

questions.question: In Psalms 115, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
questions.explanation: The very first instruction in the chapter is to 'give glory' to the LORD's name as seen in Psalms 115:1.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 115 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 115 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 115:7, what are some actions that idols cannot perform?
options: They cannot handle, walk, or speak
They cannot see, hear, or smell
questions.correctAnswer: They cannot handle, walk, or speak
questions.explanation: Psalms 115:7 states that idols have hands but do not handle, feet but do not walk, and do not speak through their throat, showing their impotence.

questions.question: What does Psalms 115:8 say about those who make idols and those who trust in them?
options: They are like the idols themselves
questions.correctAnswer: They are like the idols themselves
questions.explanation: Psalms 115:8 explains that those who make idols and those who trust in them are like the idols — powerless and without true help.

questions.question: In Psalms 115:9, whom is Israel encouraged to trust in, and what is He described as?
options: Trust in the king; a mighty warrior
Trust in the LORD; their help and shield
Trust in their leaders; their strength
Trust in their wisdom; their guide
questions.correctAnswer: Trust in the LORD; their help and shield
questions.explanation: Psalms 115:9 commands Israel to trust in the LORD, who is described as their help and shield, emphasizing God's protection and support.

questions.question: According to Psalms 115:10, what is the house of Aaron urged to do and why?
options: Build altars; to honor their ancestors
Trust in the LORD; He is their help and shield
questions.correctAnswer: Trust in the LORD; He is their help and shield
questions.explanation: Psalms 115:10 instructs the house of Aaron to trust in the LORD because He is their help and shield, highlighting reliance on God for protection.

questions.question: How does Psalms 115:11 describe those who fear the LORD in relation to trust?
options: They are commanded to trust in the LORD as their help and shield
They are to fear man more than God
They should build idols as a sign of trust
They are to separate from others
questions.correctAnswer: They are commanded to trust in the LORD as their help and shield
questions.explanation: Psalms 115:11 calls on those who fear the LORD to trust in Him, reaffirming that God is their help and shield, emphasizing faith and dependence.

questions.question: What promise is given in Psalms 115:12 about the LORD's attitude towards His people?
options: The LORD will forget His people
The LORD will be mindful and bless Israel and Aaron's house
The LORD will give them land and wealth
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD will be mindful and bless Israel and Aaron's house
questions.explanation: Psalms 115:12 assures that the LORD has been mindful of His people and will bless them, including the house of Israel and the house of Aaron.

questions.question: Based on Psalms 115:9-11, what biblical virtue is emphasized through the repeated command to trust in the LORD?
questions.explanation: Verses 9 through 11 repeatedly command Israel, the house of Aaron, and those who fear the LORD to trust in Him, highlighting the virtue of faith and dependence on God.

questions.question: What does Psalms 115:8 imply about the consequences of trusting in idols rather than in God?
options: One gains power like the idols
One becomes like the powerless idols
questions.correctAnswer: One becomes like the powerless idols
questions.explanation: Psalms 115:8 says those who make idols and trust in them are like the idols themselves—lifeless and powerless, teaching the consequence of misplaced trust.

questions.question: What does Psalms 115:12 promise will happen if the house of Israel and the house of Aaron trust in the LORD as instructed in verses 9 and 10?
options: They will be forgotten by God
They will be blessed by the LORD
They will receive earthly riches only
questions.correctAnswer: They will be blessed by the LORD
questions.explanation: Verses 9 and 10 instruct trust in the LORD, and verse 12 promises that because of this, God will be mindful and bless the house of Israel and Aaron.

questions.question: How does Psalms 115:13 expand on the blessing promised to those who fear the LORD?
options: Both small and great will be blessed
questions.correctAnswer: Both small and great will be blessed
questions.explanation: Psalms 115:13 states that God will bless all who fear Him, regardless of status, both small and great, emphasizing God's inclusive blessing.

questions.question: According to Psalms 115:14, what is the LORD's promise concerning the future of the faithful and their children?
options: The LORD shall increase you and your children more and more
The LORD will take away your offspring
The LORD will give you wealth but no children
The LORD will make your children strangers
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD shall increase you and your children more and more
questions.explanation: Psalms 115:14 promises growth and increase for the faithful and their children, indicating God's care for successive generations.

questions.question: What does Psalms 115:15 say about the source of blessing for God's people?
options: They are blessed by their own efforts
They are blessed of the LORD who made heaven and earth
They are blessed by their leaders
questions.correctAnswer: They are blessed of the LORD who made heaven and earth
questions.explanation: Psalms 115:15 attributes blessing to the LORD, the Creator of heaven and earth, emphasizing God's sovereignty as the source of blessing.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 115:7, idols can speak through their throat and walk.
questions.explanation: Psalms 115:7 explicitly says idols have hands but do not handle, feet but do not walk, and do not speak through their throat, showing their inability to act or communicate.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 115:9-11 teaches that trusting in the LORD provides help and protection to those who fear Him.
questions.explanation: Verses 9 through 11 repeatedly state that trusting in the LORD is essential because He is their help and shield, providing protection to those who fear Him.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 115:12 indicates that the LORD will forget the house of Israel and the house of Aaron despite their trust.
questions.explanation: Psalms 115:12 clearly states that the LORD has been mindful of His people and will bless both the house of Israel and the house of Aaron, showing His faithfulness.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 115 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 115.

questions.question: According to Psalms 115:13, whom will the LORD bless?
options: Both small and great who fear the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Both small and great who fear the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 115:13 explicitly states that the LORD will bless those who fear Him, both small and great, indicating no distinction in status.

questions.question: What promise is given in Psalms 115:14 regarding descendants?
options: The LORD will protect only the firstborn
The LORD shall increase you and your children more and more
The LORD will take away children as a punishment
The LORD will bless only the children of Aaron
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD shall increase you and your children more and more
questions.explanation: The verse affirms God's blessing includes growth and increase not just for the present generation but for their descendants as well.

questions.question: In Psalms 115:15, who is described as blessed by the LORD?
options: Those blessed of the LORD which made heaven and earth
questions.correctAnswer: Those blessed of the LORD which made heaven and earth
questions.explanation: The verse declares that the people who are blessed are those favored by the LORD, the Creator of heaven and earth.

questions.question: According to Psalms 115:16, what has the LORD given to the children of men?
questions.explanation: The verse contrasts the heavens, which belong to the LORD, with the earth, which He has given to mankind.

questions.question: Psalms 115:17 states that the dead do not do what?
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states that the dead, those who go down into silence, do not praise the LORD.

questions.question: What is the response of the living according to Psalms 115:18?
options: We will bless the LORD from this time forth and for evermore
questions.correctAnswer: We will bless the LORD from this time forth and for evermore
questions.explanation: The verse expresses a commitment to continually bless and praise the LORD forever.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of God as Creator and giver of the earth as found in Psalms 115:15-16?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 40:28 speaks of the LORD as the everlasting God, creator of the ends of the earth, paralleling the Creator theme in Psalms 115:15-16.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Psalms 115:4-8 when describing idols?
questions.explanation: Verses 4-8 use synonymous parallelism to emphasize the idols’ inability to speak, see, hear, or act, highlighting their powerlessness.

questions.question: In the original Hebrew, the word translated as 'bless' in Psalms 115:13 carries which nuanced meaning?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'barak' used here means to confer favor, prosperity, or well-being, not merely to praise.

questions.question: According to Psalms 115:9-11, who is repeatedly called to trust in the LORD?
options: Israel, the house of Aaron, and those who fear the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Israel, the house of Aaron, and those who fear the LORD
questions.explanation: The verses form a triad calling Israel, Aaron’s house, and all who fear God to trust in Him.

questions.question: What is the significance of the phrase 'he is their help and their shield' repeated in Psalms 115:9-11?
options: It is a metaphor for God’s protection and assistance
It describes the physical armor used by priests
It is a call for military action
It refers to a pagan ritual
questions.correctAnswer: It is a metaphor for God’s protection and assistance
questions.explanation: The phrase signifies God's role as protector and helper for those who trust in Him.

questions.question: Which earlier Psalm shares a similar refrain about idols being powerless as found in Psalms 115:4-8?
questions.explanation: Psalm 135:15-18 also describes idols as having mouths but not speaking, eyes but not seeing, paralleling the theme in Psalms 115.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 115:17 teaches that those who have died continue to praise the LORD in the afterlife.
questions.explanation: Psalms 115:17 states that the dead do not praise the LORD, indicating silence after death.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 115:18 affirms a continuous commitment by the living to bless the LORD forever.
questions.explanation: The verse clearly expresses that from now on and forevermore, the living will bless the LORD.

questions.question: How does Psalms 115:12 reflect the historical context of the Levitical priesthood?
options: It condemns the house of Aaron for idolatry
It affirms God's blessing specifically on Israel and the house of Aaron
It focuses solely on the monarchy
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms God's blessing specifically on Israel and the house of Aaron
questions.explanation: The verse highlights the LORD's mindfulness and blessings upon Israel and Aaron’s priestly lineage, important in the ancient Near Eastern religious context.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 115 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 115 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Psalms 115:1 encourage believers to give glory to?
questions.explanation: Psalms 115:1 states, 'Not unto us, O LORD, not unto us, but unto thy name give glory,' emphasizing that glory should be directed to the LORD alone for His mercy and truth.

questions.question: According to Psalms 115:2, what do the heathen question about God?
questions.explanation: The verse asks, 'Wherefore should the heathen say, Where is now their God?', indicating the skepticism of the heathen regarding God's presence.

questions.question: What is stated about God's sovereignty in Psalms 115:3?
questions.explanation: Psalms 115:3 asserts, 'But our God is in the heavens: he hath done whatsoever he hath pleased,' demonstrating God's supreme authority and action.

questions.question: What materials are mentioned as being used to make idols in Psalms 115:4?
questions.explanation: Psalms 115:4 specifies that idols are 'the work of men's hands' made of 'silver and gold', highlighting their artificial nature.

questions.question: According to Psalms 115:8, what is said about those who make idols?
questions.explanation: Psalms 115:8 states, 'They that make them are like unto them; so is every one that trusteth in them,' indicating the spiritual blindness of idolaters.

questions.question: What does Psalms 115:9 urge Israel to do?
questions.explanation: Psalms 115:9 says, 'O Israel, trust thou in the LORD: he is their help and their shield,' calling Israel to put their faith in God.

questions.question: Which group is specifically mentioned in Psalms 115:10 as needing to trust in the LORD?
questions.explanation: Psalms 115:10 addresses the 'O house of Aaron, trust in the LORD: he is their help and their shield,' indicating the priestly lineage's need for trust in God.

questions.question: What does Psalms 115:12 say about God's attention towards His people?
questions.explanation: Psalms 115:12 states, 'The LORD hath been mindful of us: he will bless us,' affirming God's ongoing concern and intention to bless His people.

questions.question: What promise is given in Psalms 115:14 regarding blessings?
questions.explanation: Psalms 115:13 declares, 'He will bless them that fear the LORD, both small and great,' emphasizing that God's blessings are for all who revere Him.

questions.question: According to Psalms 115:16, what has the LORD given to humanity?
questions.explanation: Psalms 115:16 states, 'but the earth hath he given to the children of men,' indicating God's delegation of stewardship over the earth to humanity.

questions.question: What is affirmed about the dead in Psalms 115:17?
questions.explanation: Psalms 115:17 states, 'The dead praise not the LORD, neither any that go down into silence,' indicating that praise is reserved for the living.

questions.question: What is the concluding declaration of Psalms 115:18?
questions.explanation: Psalms 115:18 concludes with, 'But we will bless the LORD from this time forth and for evermore,' committing to ongoing praise of God.

questions.question: What does Psalms 115:3 reveal about God's nature?
questions.explanation: Psalms 115:3 illustrates God's sovereignty: 'he hath done whatsoever he hath pleased,' affirming His absolute authority over all creation.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Psalms 115:9 and 115:11 convey about trusting God?
options: Trust is only for the rich
Trusting God is a collective duty
questions.correctAnswer: Trusting God is a collective duty
questions.explanation: Both verses express the necessity of trusting in the LORD: 'O Israel, trust thou in the LORD' (115:9) and 'Ye that fear the LORD, trust in the LORD' (115:11), highlighting a communal aspect.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God does not intervene in human affairs. What does Psalms 115:12-14 actually teach?
options: God does not care about humanity
questions.explanation: Psalms 115:12-14 teaches that 'The LORD hath been mindful of us: he will bless us,' affirming that God is actively involved in blessing His people, contrary to sceptical claims.
